title: Ruminant digestive system
text:
Nutrition | Mostly dependent on forages. | Mostly from concentrates, meat by-products.
Animal classification | Cattle, goat, sheep, deer, buffalo | Dogs, cats, pigs, horses and poultry
Stomach | Complex stomach consist of four compartments | Simple stomach

[Illustration: Ruminant digestive system]
Labels in diagram:
- ESOPHAGUS
- RETICULUM
- RUMEN
- OMASUM
- ABOMASUM
- SMALL INTESTINE
- LARGE INTESTINE

images.description: Anatomical diagram of a cow showing the internal pathway of the ruminant digestive system including the esophagus, rumen, reticulum, omasum, abomasum, small intestine, and large intestine.

facts: Ruminant nutrition is mostly dependent on forages.
Non-ruminant/monogastric nutrition is mostly from concentrates and meat by-products.
Animals classified under ruminants include cattle, goat, sheep, deer, and buffalo.
Animals classified under simple-stomached (non-ruminant) animals include dogs, cats, pigs, horses, and poultry.
The ruminant stomach is a complex stomach consisting of four compartments.
The four compartments of the ruminant stomach shown in the digestive system diagram are the Rumen, Reticulum, Omasum, and Abomasum.
The pathway of the ruminant digestive tract includes the Esophagus, Rumen, Reticulum, Omasum, Abomasum, Small Intestine, and Large Intestine.
